text:
maya: Heads up — noticed L4 runs slower than A100/H100 for long-seq attention in production canary. p95 token latency up ~1.8x. Logs + microbench below.

maya: microbench command:
```
./bench_attn --model=gpt-3.0 --seq=4096 --batch=1 --kernel=auto --iter=100
```

maya: output sample:
```
seq=4096 iter=100 tokens/s=2200 p95=420ms
```

ian: :eyes: that's surprising. Can you paste p50/p95 for A100/H100 run same config?

maya: A100 p95=230ms, H100 p95=210ms. L4 is the outlier.

devon: could be SM capability gating picking a more generic attention kernel for L4. We probe for sm_major >=8 && sm_minor>=9 etc. I'll dump probe logic.

devon: probe snippet:
```
if (gpu.sm >= SM_V8_0 && supports_tensor_cores()) select_fast_attn();
else select_generic_attn();
```

sophie: Maybe the probe mis-reports "supports_tensor_cores()" on L4 due to driver quirk, falling back. Also check kernel naming: we have kernels like attn_fast_sm80, attn_fast_sm90, attn_generic — maybe L4 maps to sm86 and we don't have attn_fast_sm86 built.

raj: Agree. We should emit a metric runtime.attn.kernel_selected{kernel_variant} and increment in hot path. Then run a short duration canary traffic to confirm.

kevin: We can also add an override in config: "ATTN_KERNEL_FORCE=attn_fast_sm80" to force selection for debug. I'll push a small canary that sets that env for the L4 pool.

ops-bot: ci/build/attn_kernels: succeeded (artifact: attn_fast_sm80.so)

maya: I'll run the forced-canary and post numbers in ~10m.

(10m later)

maya: forced canary numbers: L4 with ATTN_KERNEL_FORCE=attn_fast_sm80 p95=215ms — matches H100/A100. So it's definitely selector/build mismatch.

devon: root cause: our build matrix only produced attn_fast for sm80 and sm90. L4 reports sm86; we didn't produce attn_fast_sm86 binary. Fixes:
- add sm86 target in kernel build
- augment probe to map sm86->sm80 path if feature set compatible
- emit metric to detect when mapping/override is used

sophie: tradeoffs: mapping reduces binary count but hides real capability differences. Building per-sm increases CI time and artifact storage. Suggest: build generic and one optimized per family (sm80 family -> sm80 vs sm90 family), and have runtime probe map family.

raj: Also need rollout plan: canary -> 24h perf monitoring -> promote. Add regression alert if p95 delta >15% per model.

kevin: I'll open a small RFC for build matrix update and a runtime-mapping change. Tagging @eng-runtime @arch for review.

maya: thanks. I'll close the incident. :thumbsup:
